findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define detector behavior for ungrouped/short ticket-id citation forms (concatenated hex, prefix, or 'rebar:<id>' token) — either normalize them into the accepted-alias class or explicitly document them as out-of-scope — and add a unit test pinning that decision.
evidence: Plan defines accepted alias forms only as 'hex-grouped or word-triple alias'

Ticket ids appear in the tree in grouped form ('3006-e198-13db-4e1f') but the reducer/citation tokens also use forms like 'rebar:3006-e198' and short prefixes; an ungrouped 16-hex id matches the SHA rule (>=7 hex, digits+letters)
The plan's own test gotchas cover grouped-4x4 and word-triple accepts but are silent on ungrouped/short id forms
findings.finding: The rot-prone SHA rule ('SHA-like hex >=7 with digits+letters') and the accepted alias forms ('hex-grouped 4x4' or 'word-triple') do not define behavior for a bare, ungrouped full ticket id (e.g. '3006e19813db4e1f') or a short/prefix id. Such an ungrouped id is 16 hex with digits+letters and would trip the SHA rule, producing either a false positive or an under-specified accept path.
findings.location: Approach step (2): "rot-prone = SHA-like hex >=7 with digits+letters ... ACCEPTED when the block cites a ticket/epic/story/bug/rec/ADR id (hex-grouped or word-triple alias)"
scenarios: A comment cites a ticket by its concatenated 16-hex id; the detector flags it as a rot-prone SHA (false positive) or the acceptor fails to recognize it
A short-form/prefix ticket reference is neither accepted-as-alias nor clearly rejected

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the guard handles a block that BOTH cites a ticket id AND contains a rot-prone token: either scope acceptance to the rationale (not a blanket whole-block pass) or add a line-level residual check that still rejects a rot-prone SHA/run-id unless it carries the 'context: external' escape hatch.
evidence: Plan: 'ACCEPTED when the block cites a ticket/epic/story/bug/rec/ADR id — pointing history at the ticket system is the sanctioned pattern'
src/rebar/_config_schema.py:399-401 — the date-verb sentence '2026-07-03 census measured 1.14% acting' is NOT flagged solely because 'epic 3006-e198' sits in the same comment run
search: 'epic 3006-e198' appears in 30+ comment/docstring blocks across src/ and tests/, so almost any block can be made 'accepted'
AC-2 requires the guard to fail on reintroduced rot-prone refs, but whole-block acceptance lets a rot-prone SHA ride along inside a ticket-citing block
findings.finding: The CI guard's ACCEPT rule is whole-block: a comment/docstring block that cites any ticket/epic/story/bug/ADR id is accepted in its entirety, so a rot-prone SHA co-located in the same block passes the guard. Because the reconciler pervasively cites 'epic 3006-e198' (dozens of blocks), a reintroduced dead SHA placed in any ticket-citing block would not be caught — weakening the guard's fitness for the named purpose (SHAs rot).
findings.location: Approach step (2): "ACCEPTED when the block cites a ticket/epic/story/bug/rec/ADR id"; Acceptance Criteria line 2 ("CI guard fails on reintroduced rot-prone refs")
scenarios: A future edit adds a fresh commit SHA into an existing docstring that already cites 'epic 3006-e198'; the guard accepts the whole block and the SHA rots undetected
Author satisfies the guard by pasting a ticket id next to an otherwise rot-prone incident narrative
findings.suggested_fix: Make ACCEPT narrower: a ticket cite suppresses the date+evidence-verb heuristic (history-at-ticket is legitimate) but does NOT suppress a bare SHA-like hex run or run/thread-id — those must be removed or escape-hatched even in a ticket-citing block. Add a detector unit test: a block containing both 'epic 3006-e198' and a live 40-char SHA must still be RED.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the detector's ACCEPTED-arm id/alias recognition reuses or references rebar's canonical grammar (src/rebar/_ids.py / det_citation.py _CITATION_RE / invariants.py _TICKET_ID_RE) rather than re-deriving it, and note any deliberate divergences (e.g. accepting word-prefixed epic/story/bug/rec/ADR forms).
evidence: Canonical grammar already exists: src/rebar/_ids.py '_FULL_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9]{4}$")' + _SHORT_ID_RE, documented as 'the single resolution seam ... so every surface accepts the same ID forms'.

src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_citation.py:40-43 encodes the same thing: '<ticket-id> matches rebar's id/alias grammar (:mod:`rebar._ids`): a full/short lowercase-hex id (`[a-z0-9]{4}-...`) OR an adjective-noun-noun alias'.
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/invariants.py:36 '_TICKET_ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}\b")'.
The plan names the accepted forms only in prose ('hex-grouped or word-triple alias') and does not mention any of these existing definitions.

ANTI-FP: this is coached (not asserted NIH) because the detector scans free-text comments/docstrings and accepts extra word-prefixed forms (epic/story/bug/rec/ADR), so the canonical [rebar:...]-token regex may not be a clean drop-in — reuse-vs-reference is the open question.
findings.finding: The detector's ACCEPTED-arm ticket-ID/alias grammar re-derives a shape that already has a canonical definition in the codebase, without referencing or reusing it — a drift risk (the guard and the real resolver can diverge on what counts as a valid id/alias).
findings.location: Approach, step (2): 'ACCEPTED when the block cites a ticket/epic/story/bug/rec/ADR id (hex-grouped or word-triple alias)'
scenarios: The alias generator changes (e.g. the _alias.py v1 adj-noun-noun vs v2 adj-adj-animal note) and the hand-rolled detector grammar silently stops accepting valid new aliases, producing false-positive CI failures.
A contributor cites a valid short-id (8-hex) form that _ids.py accepts but the detector's hand-rolled 'hex-grouped' pattern was written for the 16-hex form only.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, point the acceptor arm at the existing canonical grammar (import from or mirror rebar._ids / det_citation._CITATION_RE) and explicitly enumerate the intended supersets (word-prefixed epic/story/bug/rec/ADR aliases) so reviewers can see the delta from canonical is deliberate, not accidental drift.
